A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Russian Federation is not a unitary state.
the center has been able to influence the bargaining process in the Russian Federation by offering regional leaders structural power.
regional leaders in regions with structural power were able to use their resources to gain concessions from the center in bilateral treaty negotiations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Russian bilateral treaty process has not been a zero-sum game.

the bilateral treaty process was a bargaining game between the center and regions, in which regions with structural power resources could bargain better and get a favorable deal in their bilateral treaties.
the structural power resources of regions are of crucial importance to understand the dynamics of center-region relations in Russia.
